answer.rationale: Rollback (memory_b1) is off the table: compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible, so the one precedent with the cleanest track record is unavailable regardless of how well it worked on day 18. That leaves two live candidates. Regional failover (memory_b2) matches the topology signal well  ailregion region, degradation confined there i and is the only intervention that fully removes the primary from the hot path, but the March precedent recorded latency recovery, not write durability, and it says nothing about whether traffic was write-heavy at the time. Shifting the write path mid-settlement-peak is exactly the condition under which cutover risks in-flight write loss, and the primary objective explicitly protects customer writes  iso b2's success cannot be assumed to transfer. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) is the lowest-blast-radius option: it relieves the primary without touching the write path at all, and it is trivially reversible if it does nothing. Its weakness is mechanism mismatch  i b5 offloaded dashboard/report queries, while today's load is settlement writes; if read contention is not a material contributor, the relief will be small. I verify b5 and b2 precisely to resolve these two questions: whether b5's relief came from generic primary-load reduction (transfers) or a dashboard-specific quirk (does not), and whether b2's failover was executed under heavy writes with any write-loss accounting. I commit now to read-replica routing as a small guarded test with explicit latency and queue-depth checkpoints; if verification shows b5's mechanism was narrow, or the guarded test fails to bend p99, failover with a deliberate write drain becomes the next-window action rather than something improvised under peak. Add-capacity (b3) and circuit breakers (b4) are noted but weaker fits: b3's precedent was pre-provisioning ahead of a known peak, not mid-incident, and b4 addressed a partner dependency failure, which is not the observed signal  ifailing fast on our own primary would shed exactly the customer writes we are told to protect. Value risk flagged: the memory set is uniformly success-framed with sources archived and no recorded failures or base rates, so it likely over-represents interventions that happened to work and cannot tell me how often failover lost writes under load.
